internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 38 occurrences the root ف ت ح contributes one motivated idea: un-closing what was shut. The physical prototype is opening a container or a gate (baggage 12:65; gates of the sky 15:14, 54:11, 78:19; gates of Hell and Paradise 39:71, 39:73). From this the Quran extends the same act along transparent axes: 'to open upon' someone = to release/bestow/disclose what was withheld (mercy 35:2, blessings 7:96, gates of everything as istidraj 6:44, disclosed knowledge 2:76); and 'to open between parties with truth' = to render a decisive verdict resolving a standoff (7:89, 34:26, 26:118). The nominal al-fatH names that decisive outcome/breakthrough (48:1, 110:1, 61:13, the day of decision 32:29), sought via form X istaftaHa (8:19, 2:89, 14:15), and mafatiH is the derived instrument ('keys') of access (6:59, 24:61). The internal anchor is 35:2, where fatH is set explicitly against imsak (withholding) and paired with irsal (release), fixing the nucleus as 'un-withhold / un-close' rather than crude physical 'open'.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ftH does NOT mean: (1) help/aid — fatH is conjoined-but-distinct from naSr in 110:1 and 61:13, so it is the decisive outcome, not the assistance; (2) generic decree/command — disjoined from amr in 5:52; (3) general legal judgment (Hukm) — fataHa bayna is reserved for the vindicating verdict between a prophet-community and its opponents, always +bi-l-Haqq, narrower than yaHkumu (which appears separately in 4:141); (4) creation ex nihilo — what is opened pre-exists behind a barrier (water 54:11, mercy 35:2, treasures behind keys 28:76); (5) destruction/breaking — the closure is undone, not smashed (78:19 sky becomes gates; 12:65 baggage opened intact); (6) generic giving (ata) — it is giving by opening a channel (7:96 barakat through opened gates). It is also valence-neutral: the same act opens gates of Paradise (39:73) and of punishment (23:77) and of istidraj (6:44). No verse takes a city/land as object, so 'military conquest' is contextual, not a lexical entailment.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 28:76:14:1 (Qarun): 'inna mafatiHahu latanuu bi-l-Uzbati uli l-quwwati' — the referent is heavy hoarded wealth that weighs down a band of strong men. Read as 'hoards/treasure-stores' the token denotes a mass of goods, not an act of opening, and even 'keys' strains (keys do not weigh down strongmen); the un-closing component is fully bleached. The only route back to the nucleus is a two-step, Quran-undemonstrated metonymy (open -> key -> what the key guards -> treasure); the packet nowhere states that keys open stores. This is a genuine lexicalized concrete nominal that the packet cannot bridge, and it forbids a STRONG/UNIVERSAL verdict.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Homonymy / lexical split: treat (1) physical OPEN (A/B), (2) ADJUDICATE (fataHa bayna, al-fattaH), and (3) VICTORY (nominal al-fatH, istaftaHa), plus the concrete nominal mafatiH, as separately-listed conventionalized senses glued only by shared consonants. Rebuttal (Quran-internal): the event-senses are demonstrably continuous, not homonymous — 8:19 puts istaftaHa and the noun al-fatH in one clause (same event named by verb and noun); 32:29 yawma l-fatH is simultaneously verdict (faith will not avail the deniers) and decisive triumph; 6:44 carries bestowal through the physical 'gates' image, fusing A and B; and 35:2 supplies the antonym yumsik, fixing one nucleus 'un-withhold/un-close' that subsumes bestowal, verdict, and victory. The homonymy account cannot explain these seams; a single nucleus with lexicalized nodes predicts them. However, the lexicalization of mafatiH (esp. 28:76) is real, so the competitor is not fully refuted for that nominal — which is exactly why the grade is capped, not why the unified event-claim is abandoned.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converge on one motivated nucleus ('decisive un-closing / un-withholding') with internally-attested bridges: 35:2 (fatH vs imsak, the definitional anchor), 6:44 (A->B: literal gates carrying abstract grant), 8:19 (F->C: istaftaHa and al-fatH in one clause), 32:29 (C<->D: verdict and triumph in one word), 2:76 (disclosure of knowledge). candidate_root_contribution: To undo a pre-existing closure: to move something from a shut, withheld, or unresolved state into openness, so that it becomes accessible, released, disclosed, or decisively resolved. The root presupposes (a) a prior state of closure/withholding/undecidedness and (b) an agent (overwhelmingly God) who removes it; it does not create, break, or merely give.

rejection_condition.confounder_control: Do not treat shared root consonants or a shared English gloss ('open') as evidence of one sense; require an actual Quran-internal alternation or antonymy linking the classes, and exclude contextual/narrative meaning (e.g. 'the Conquest of Mecca') from the root claim.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If the mafatiH and/or bayna classes are shown genuinely unbridged, the unified REPRESENTATIVE claim is downgraded to UNRESOLVED (UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY) with ftH partitioned into distinct lexicalized classes rather than one nucleus.

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal reading fixes 28:76 mafatiHahu decisively as 'keys' (instrument) rather than 'hoards', re-examine whether Cluster E is fully CONSISTENT and whether the grade can move toward STRONG.

If further analysis shows the fataHa bayna...bi-l-Haqq frame (7:89, 34:26, 26:118) plus al-fattaH/al-fatiHin cannot be bridged to the release/disclosure nucleus, re-partition ftH toward a distinct lexicalized 'adjudicate' class and downgrade scope.

If the naSr+fatH conjunction (110:1, 61:13) or the fatH/amr disjunction (5:52) is re-read as identity rather than distinctness, revisit the semantic_boundary claims that fatH != help and fatH != decree.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The core nucleus is broad, internally anchored (35:2 imsak/irsal antonymy), and distinctiveness holds (fatH != naSr in 110:1/61:13; fatH != amr in 5:52; fataHa bayna != generic yaHkumu in 4:141). A full adversarial refutation is not marked PASSED because a coherent resistant lexicalized member persists (28:76); per contract the core holds while the resistant occurrence is recorded rather than treated as a global refutation.
